case_number: Criminal Appeal No. of 2024 (Arising out of SLP(Crl.)No.4887 of 2024) and Criminal Appeal No. of 2024 (Arising out of SLP(Crl.)No.7896 of 2023)
summary: The appeals challenged the Kerala High Court's order quashing criminal proceedings in Crime No.215/1994 and C.C. No.811/2014 for offenses under IPC Sections 120B, 420, 201, 193, 217, and 34, relating to alleged tampering with evidence (Mo2) in a prior NDPS case. The High Court applied the bar under Section 195(1)(b) CrPC, requiring prior court permission for prosecution, and quashed proceedings while directing de novo action under that provision. The Supreme Court considered whether M.R. Ajayan, a public-spirited citizen and journalist, had locus standi to challenge the quashing; whether the bar under Section 195(1)(b) CrPC rightly applied; and whether the High Court could direct fresh proceedings after quashing. The Court examined precedents on public interest locus in criminal matters and the procedural requirements for invoking Section 195.
legal_provisions_cited: Section 195(1)(b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
Section 20(b)(ii) of the Narcotics Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
Article 136 of the Constitution of India
P.S.R. Sadhanantham v. Arunachalam & Anr. (1980) 3 SCC 141
National Commission for Women v. State of Delhi & Anr.
Amanuallah & Anr. v. State of Bihar & Ors.
final_judgment: Leave granted; issues framed and matters listed for detailed hearing on merits.
